user:
Research problem: Can MVFA's few-shot fusion be made inductive — scoring each image on its own, without the test-set min-max normalisation of the released code — without losing AUROC, and does this give a threshold that transfers to unseen modalities? The inductive fusion standardises each branch with leave-one-out statistics of the K normal support images (each support's zero-shot map, and its few-shot map against a memory bank built from the other K-1 supports, pooled over patches and levels), adds the standardised branches, and pools the fused map with the mean of its top 2% pixels; the threshold is the 95th percentile of the supports' leave-one-out image scores. Primary outcome: image- and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive fusion on every held-out modality and K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the transductive AUROC across random test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Secondary outcomes: sensitivity, realised specificity, F1 and expected calibration error at the support-derived threshold. We also record whether the few-shot baselines compared in the target paper (APRIL-GAN, WinCLIP) normalise over the test set in their public code, to judge how widely the finding applies.

Below are 24 candidate research ideas for this problem. Group them into 4-7 method families such that ideas in the same family share their core mechanism (not merely their goal). Give each family a short name.

[B1-g0-C1] Bounded leave-one-out z-score fusion (LOO-Z) for per-image MVFA scoring
Standardise MVFA's zero-shot and few-shot maps with leave-one-out statistics of the K support normals, clip them to a bounded range, fuse with inverse-variance weights and pool the top 2% pixels, so every image is scored on its own.

[B1-g0-C2] Empirical p-value fusion across levels and branches (Fisher-MVFA)
Turn each level/branch patch score into an empirical p-value against support-normal LOO scores and combine them with Fisher's method, giving a per-image, distribution-free anomaly statistic and a principled threshold.

[B1-g0-C3] Support-synthesised Platt calibration for inductive MVFA fusion
Create synthetic anomalies on the K support normals, fit a two-feature logistic calibrator (zero-shot and few-shot image scores) on support normals versus their synthetic versions, and use it to score each test image without test-set statistics.

[B1-g0-C4] Shrinkage-Gaussian Mahalanobis scoring of support normals for inductive few-shot fusion
Replace the few-shot branch's max-cosine memory search with per-level Mahalanobis distances under a Ledoit-Wolf Gaussian fitted to support patch features, standardise by its chi-square reference, and fuse per image with the zero-shot branch.

[B1-g0-C5] Region-mass aggregation: scoring images by their strongest coherent anomalous region
Threshold each image's per-image-normalised fused map at a support-derived pixel level, extract connected regions, and score the image by the best region's mean score weighted by log area, replacing the max-pixel rule.

[B1-g0-C6] Causal streaming normalisation of MVFA branch scores from confidently normal arrivals
Initialise branch normalisation from the support normals and update robust statistics (median/MAD) online using only incoming images scored below the current threshold, compared against support-only and test-set normalisation.

[B1-g1-o1] Gaussian-standardised few-shot branch with LOO-Z zero-shot fusion and region-mass pooling
Score each image on its own by fusing an analytically standardised Mahalanobis few-shot map with a support-standardised zero-shot map and pooling the result by its strongest coherent region.

[B1-g1-o2] LOO-Z inductive fusion with region-mass image scoring and a single support-derived operating point
Combine bounded leave-one-out z-score fusion of MVFA's two branches with region-mass image aggregation, and derive both pixel and image thresholds from the K support normals only.

[B1-g1-o3] Intra-image robust normalisation: each image as its own normal reference for per-image MVFA scoring
Normalise every patch score of an image by the robust statistics (median and MAD) of that same image's patch scores, exploiting that most patches of any image are normal, and combine with a support-derived threshold.

[B1-g1-o4] Episode-trained fusion calibrator: learning how to fuse MVFA's branches from simulated few-shot episodes on source modalities
Learn, on simulated K-shot episodes drawn from the source modalities' validation splits, a small calibrator that maps support statistics and per-image branch scores to an anomaly probability, then apply it unchanged to the unseen target modality.

[B1-g1-o5] Image-versus-support two-sample testing: deciding each image by an MMD test against the support normals' patch distribution
Treat each test image's adapted patch tokens as a sample and test whether it comes from the same distribution as the support normals' patches with a kernel MMD statistic and a permutation p-value, giving a per-image, calibrated decision without test-set normalisation.

[B1-g1-o6] Extreme-value tail calibration of MVFA branch scores from support normals
Fit a generalised Pareto distribution to the upper tail of each branch's support-normal LOO patch scores and convert test scores to tail probabilities, giving per-image scores that remain discriminative beyond the range seen in the supports.

[B1-g2-o1] Episode-calibrated weighted Fisher fusion: learning per-level weights of support p-values on source-modality episodes
Compute per-level, per-branch empirical p-values against the target's support normals (inductive, distribution-free) and combine them with weights and a logistic mapping learned on simulated K-shot episodes from the source modalities' labelled validation images.

[B1-g2-o2] Neyman-Pearson likelihood-ratio scoring: a support-normal density against a cross-modality abnormal density learned on source data
Score each test patch by the log-ratio between a density of 'generic abnormal' patch features learned from source modalities' abnormal images and a density of the target's support-normal patches, giving the most powerful per-image test at a chosen false-positive level.

[B1-g2-o3] Nearest-source-modality calibration transfer: calibrating an unseen modality with the source modalities its supports resemble
Measure how similar the target's support normals are to each source modality in adapted feature space, and transfer the score-to-probability calibration learned on source episodes with weights proportional to that similarity.

[B1-g2-o4] Risk-controlled abstention band: per-image MVFA decisions that defer when support evidence is insufficient
Turn per-image MVFA scores into three-way decisions (normal, abnormal, defer) using a lower and an upper threshold calibrated on source-modality episodes to control the error rate on non-deferred images, reporting risk-coverage curves instead of a single AUROC.

[B1-g2-o5] Adaptive S-norm for MVFA: cohort score normalisation borrowed from speaker verification
Normalise each test image's anomaly score both against the target supports (Z-norm) and against how the same image scores against memory banks built from a cohort of other modalities' normal images (T-norm), and average the two, as speaker-verification systems do to make one threshold work across speakers.

[B1-g2-o6] Harmonic-mean p-value fusion with region-mass scoring: per-image MVFA scores that stay valid under dependent levels
Replace Fisher's combination, which assumes independent evidence, with the harmonic mean p-value across MVFA's strongly correlated levels and branches, keeping region-mass pooling and support-derived thresholds.

[B1-g3-o1] FDR-controlled anomaly maps: Benjamini-Yekutieli discoveries per image from support-anchored pixel p-values
Treat every patch of a test image as a hypothesis test against the support normals, apply the Benjamini-Yekutieli procedure (valid under dependence) at a target false discovery rate, and score the image by the mass of discovered patches.

[B1-g3-o2] Support-bootstrap uncertainty: deciding on the lower confidence bound of a per-image MVFA score
Resample the K support normals with replacement to obtain a distribution of each test image's support-normalised score, and flag an image only when the lower confidence bound exceeds the threshold, giving per-image uncertainty that grows as K shrinks.

[B1-g3-o3] E-value fusion: dependence-robust, betting-based per-image anomaly evidence from support normals
Convert each level/branch patch score into an e-value (a likelihood-ratio-like betting score calibrated on the support normals), average e-values across levels and branches — valid under any dependence — and decide by the e-value's guarantee P(E >= 1/alpha) <= alpha.

[B1-g3-o4] Test-time-augmentation consensus: scoring an image by anomaly evidence that survives across augmented views
Score several label-preserving augmentations of each test image with per-image p-value fusion and take the minimum (or a low quantile) of the region scores across views, so isolated spurious peaks that do not persist across views no longer decide the image label.

[B1-g3-o5] Brown-corrected Fisher fusion: dependence-adjusted p-value combination estimated from support normals, with region-mass pooling
Keep Fisher's powerful combination of per-level, per-branch support p-values but correct its null distribution for the dependence between MVFA's levels and branches using Brown's method with covariances estimated on the support normals, then pool by region mass.

[B1-g3-o6] Instance-whitened patch features: per-image scoring that is robust to acquisition shift between supports and test images
Remove per-image style statistics (channel means and variances of adapted patch tokens) before both few-shot matching and support-anchored p-values, so that differences in scanner, contrast or staining between the K supports and a test image do not masquerade as anomalies.
